description:
Problem: while develop's red streak is unreverted, the arm gate (scripts/trunk_revert.py arm_gate, :174-192) refuses every PR except a fix/revert-* branch whose commits revert the streak's first red commit. After 30 minutes, make pr-open also refuses every non-revert branch (trunk_gate, :72-104; Makefile:1213). On 2026-10-24 the right repair was a fix-forward (#3385, head 5e2fdde9d994b98a694d2891b41ef0006b8f058f, branch fix/comment-policy-notice-paths, while the streak started at Trunk run 40071232825 on 24bfcf8a0fb048c9ad554ef2e9e99066f7027167). The only way through was an owner ruleset relaxation. (The false revert identity in Advisor finding F14 was fixed by #3415: the gate now blames the first red run of the streak and exempts its genuine revert; see tests/unit/scripts/test_trunk_revert.py:573-584.)

Outcome: a narrowly authorized fix-forward path through make pr-open and the arm gate, bound to the PR number, its current head SHA and the streak's first failing Trunk run. Required checks, oracle-gate, review threads and holds still apply.

Authorization model: all agents act through the owner's GitHub account (docs/agent/merge-authority.md:16-18), so no API signal can prove the owner, rather than an agent, made it. The signal is audit-enforced, like a stand-in. It is a PR comment whose whole body is exactly 'Fix-forward authorized: <40-hex head SHA> for trunk run <run databaseId>'. It counts only when: the login is in an allowlist of joeharris76; the user type is User; the comment was never edited; it was created after the named run completed; the SHA equals the PR's current head; and the run id equals the first red run of the current streak. Agents post it only when the owner names the PR and head in the current request, after an 'Owner instruction' comment quoting that request, exactly as for stand-ins.

Decision gates:
1. Signal approval. Proceed only after the owner approves the comment format above and the opening rule in gate 3. If the owner chooses another signal, record it in context first. Stop if the chosen signal cannot be bound to head SHA and run id through the GitHub API.
2. Scope. The authorization exempts arming only; it never bypasses required checks, oracle-gate, thread resolution or holds. A new push voids it, because the SHA no longer matches.
3. Opening. make pr-open must let the fix-forward PR exist before it is authorized. Recommended: while the trunk gate would refuse, make pr-open opens the PR as a draft instead of refusing, and prints that arming needs the owner's authorization. Stop and ask if the owner prefers to keep the refusal.

Item guardrails: no unrestricted --force flag; no ruleset edits; no change to merge-authority holds; no change to who may revert. Never post a live authorization comment while implementing; tests and replays use captured fixtures only.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Do not change oracle-gate's App binding (integration 5201041), the oracle decision rule, or the native review-thread-resolution requirement. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests. No explanatory comments or docstrings in code; commits, PR bodies and docs carry no tracker item IDs or session labels; timing uses benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time().
